# Hook Types: Pre-Commit, Commit-Msg, Pre-Push

After this page you can name the client hooks this book uses and where they live on Linux.

## A hook is a program Git runs

Executable files in `.git/hooks/`. Git looks at the filename. If `pre-commit` exists and is executable (`chmod +x`), Git runs it before it writes a commit object. Exit status `0` continues. Non-zero aborts.

```text
 git commit
    │
    ▼
 pre-commit      exit ≠ 0 ──► abort, no object
    │ 0
    ▼
 commit-msg      exit ≠ 0 ──► abort, no object
    │ 0
    ▼
 commit object written, main slides forward

 git push
    │
    ▼
 pre-push        exit ≠ 0 ──► abort, remote unchanged
    │ 0
    ▼
 objects uploaded
```

Sample files are `*.sample` and are **not** run. Copy and chmod:

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
ls .git/hooks
install -m 0755 .git/hooks/pre-commit.sample .git/hooks/pre-commit
# then edit; or write your own
```

`install -m 0755` is the Linux way to copy and set the executable bit in one step.

## Client hooks you will write

| Hook | When | Typical job |
|------|------|-------------|
| `pre-commit` | After you type `git commit`, before the object exists | Lint, block secrets, `git diff --check` |
| `commit-msg` | After you save the message | Conventional Commits pattern |
| `pre-push` | After you type `git push`, before objects upload | Tests, block WIP branches |

There are more (`prepare-commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-checkout`). Start with these three.

## Server hooks (later)

A forge runs `pre-receive` / `update` / `post-receive` on the server when you push. Chapter 23 names them; chapter 31 uses them for policy. Your laptop hooks do not run on the server. A teammate can skip `pre-commit` with `git commit --no-verify`. Server hooks are the ones that actually enforce.

## Environment

Hooks run with a POSIX shell on Linux unless the shebang says otherwise. Always start with:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
```

Git sets `GIT_DIR` and runs with the working tree as cwd for client hooks (with nuances for worktrees, chapter 14). Print to stderr so you do not pollute commit output:

```bash
echo "pre-commit: running" >&2
```
